label: F-a1cbd5

findings.note: AntigravityRuntime.cs:110 at 2f2e138 routes SpentWithoutReset to Undecided, which leaves an undecided refusal unparked; that is what the plan decided (its D5 state table, 'cannot check | ... no reset_time | nothing parked for an undecided refusal').

AgyQuotaReport.cs:145-146 tries the whole trimmed stdout and then single lines that start with '{', so pretty-printed JSON behind a preamble would read as no report; but no agy preamble is observed, and the fallback is CannotCheck, which the plan handles.

QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs:53-65 at 2f2e138 catches only OperationCanceledException, so one key's unexpected failure escapes to AfterRoundAsync and drops every key's change; 20df878 adds the general catch that drops only that key.
At 2f2e138 research/architecture.md was untouched although the flow crosses the server and the extension; 20df878 adds 13 lines there, but a docs gap is minor rather than major.

Read() at 2f2e138 accepted {Entries: not null} with null elements, so Standing's entry.Key would throw past the fail-open contract; 20df878 adds TrueForAll(entry is not null); it needs a hand-corrupted file, so minor.

ChangesAsync (Round.cs:38-50) does await the keys in turn, but only agy keys probe (Codex, Claude and Kimi use the default text reading with no process), so the worst case is three 30 s agy timeouts after rounds that take minutes; the plan never asks for concurrency.
AntigravityRuntime.cs:47-64 at 20df878 builds every agy reviewer request with AntigravityReadOnly.Home() as the working folder, so the cloned probe request already runs there, as D6 specifies.

QuotaCooldowns.cs:255-256: an entry is only reordered when its key is parked or lifted, and that changes the contents and must be written anyway; a lift of an absent key keeps the order, so SequenceEqual holds and nothing is written.

Round.cs:77 and PanelService.cs:424 both call the same adapter QuotaKeyOf on the model string; Codex, Claude and Kimi return a constant, and agy already handles an empty model; the casing or null scenario is invented.
The plan's D4 decides 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever)', so QuotaCooldowns.cs:167-168 reading on every call is the spec.

AgyError.Parse only runs on the failure path of a process that has already ended, over stderr the executor has already bounded and redacted; avoiding allocations here is micro-optimisation, not a defect.
AgyQuotaProbe.cs:29 uses Timeout = 30 s and --print-timeout 20s, exactly as the plan's D6 prescribes.
ReviewerRuntime.cs:543's default QuotaKeyOf => string.Empty is the plan's D3 decision ('empty means this runtime has no quota coai parks').

D4's fail-open contract decides that an unreadable file reads as no cooldown and that no quota is parked until the file is written again (QuotaCooldowns.cs:184-219), so the next write replacing it is the designed behaviour; a v:2 file is speculative.
AgyQuotaProbe.cs:63 passes the first stderr line through VendorReason.Written, which is Redaction.SafeText (VendorReason.cs:31), the product's standard redaction, so the line is redacted.
This repeats R1#5: Round.cs:41-47 probes sequentially, but at most three agy keys probe, with a 30 s bound each, and the plan accepts minutes-scale rounds.
PanelService.cs:423-424 reads per row because D4 decides 'no cache' for a file under 16 KiB; the 1,000-row, 1,000-key scenario has no basis, since there are at most six keys.

summary: Round 1 found three real, cheap defects that the implementation then fixed in 20df878: a probe failure aborting every key's update, a null cooldown entry breaking the fail-open read, and the missing architecture.md update. Round 2 is almost all noise: findings that contradict the plan's explicit decisions (no cache, the 30 s timeout, the empty default key, fail-open) or misread the code (the working folder, redaction, SequenceEqual).
